Gut health has become a major focus in nutrition research, and while no single food is a cure-all, a handful of categories consistently show up as beneficial.

## Fermented foods

Yogurt, kefir, sauerkraut, and kimchi all introduce live cultures that can support a more diverse gut microbiome over time.

## Fiber-rich plants

Beans, oats, and a wide variety of vegetables feed the beneficial bacteria already living in your gut, which matters as much as introducing new ones.

## Foods to moderate

Highly processed foods and excess added sugar tend to favor less beneficial bacteria, so moderation here matters as much as what you actively add to your plate.

Variety appears to matter more than any single "superfood," so rotating through a wide range of plants over the course of a week is a more reliable strategy than eating the same few gut-friendly foods every day.
